findings.text: PCI Express slot and root registers live at fixed small offsets: Slot Status near 0x1a, Root Control near 0x1c, Root Capabilities near 0x1e, Root Status at 0x20. Slot Control groups command-completed and hot-plug interrupt enables, attention and power indicator selectors including on/blink/off encodings, power controller on/off, interlock, link-state-change enable, and slot power-limit plus in-band presence disables. Slot Status groups button pressed, power fault, sensor changed/state, presence changed/state, command completed, interlock status and link-state changed. Root registers group correctable/non-fatal/fatal system-error enables, PME interrupt enable, config retry visibility enable with compatibility alias, visibility capability, and PME requester identifier plus PME status and pending flags.

Device Capabilities 2, Device Control 2 and Device Status 2 live around offsets 0x24, 0x28 and 0x2a, with a version-2 root endpoint size of 0x2c. Capabilities advertise completion-timeout-disable support, alternative routing, atomic routing and 32/64/128-bit completer widths, latency reporting, completer hint support, optimized-buffering message versus WAKE signaling, and end-to-end prefix support plus maximum prefix count. Control selects timeout value and disable, alternative routing, atomic request enable and egress blocking, ordering relaxations for requests and completions, latency-report enable, and optimized-buffering message A/B versus WAKE enable encodings.

Link Capabilities 2, Link Control 2 and Link Status 2 live around offsets 0x2c, 0x30 and 0x32, with endpoint-with-link size 0x34 and Slot Capabilities 2, Slot Control 2 and Slot Status 2 around 0x34, 0x38 and 0x3a. Link Capabilities 2 carries a supported-speed vector from 2.5 through 64 GT/s plus crosslink support. Link Control 2 carries a target-speed field with encodings for the same six generations, plus enter-compliance, transmit-margin and autonomous-speed-disable controls. Link Status 2 reports flit mode. Slot Capabilities 2 reports in-band presence-disable support.

An extended capability header word is decoded into three fields: low 16 bits identify the capability, next 4 bits carry version, and the high field carries the next-pointer offset masked to dword alignment. Vendor-specific, RCEC bus-number, power-budget data and capability, and error-capability first-error-pointer values are likewise decoded by masking and shifting the register word rather than by direct equality.

Extended capability identifiers form a fixed numeric registry from 0x01 for error reporting through 0x31 for 64 GT/s physical layer, covering virtual channels, serial number, power budgeting, root-complex link and event-collector constructs, vendor-specific, access control, alternative routing, address translation, single and multi-root virtualization, multicast, page-request, resizable BAR including VF form, dynamic power, hints, latency reporting, secondary capability, multiplexing, process address space, containment, L1 substates, time measurement, designated vendor-specific, link features, enclosure management, object exchange, device-3 and encryption, with one compatibility duplicate for virtual channels and one reserved AMD value; serial-number size is 12 bytes and multicast endpoint size is 40 bytes.

Advanced error uncorrectable status and mask live at offsets 0x04 and 0x08, severity at 0x0c. Status bits distinguish link protocol, surprise down, poisoned packet, flow control, completion timeout, completer abort, unexpected completion, receiver overflow, malformed packet, end-to-end CRC, unsupported request, access-control violation, internal error, blocked multicast/atomic-with-egress/prefix/poison/write traffic, encryption check and misrouting failures, packet CRC failure, and translation-egress blocking, plus an undefined low bit.

Correctable status and mask live at offsets 0x10 and 0x14, advanced capabilities at 0x18, header log at 0x1c with 16 bytes, root command at 0x2c, root status at 0x30, error source at 0x34, prefix log at 0x38 with up to 16 bytes. Correctable bits cover receiver errors, bad packet and link packets, replay rollover and timeout, advisory non-fatal, corrected internal and log overflow. Capabilities carry first-error pointer, end-to-end CRC generation and check capability plus enable, prefix-log present, timeout log capability, flit-log indicator and logged-size field. Root command enables correctable, non-fatal and fatal reporting; root status reports received and multiple correctable and uncorrectable messages, first-fatal marker, non-fatal/fatal receipt, and interrupt message number.

Virtual-channel port registers live around offsets 0x04 through 0x0e and per-resource registers around 0x10 through 0x1a, with base size 0x10 and per-channel stride 0x0c. Port capabilities describe extended-channel count, low-priority count, arbitration-table size, supported 32/64/128-phase arbitration, and table offset; port control and status provide a load-table request and completion flag. Resource capabilities describe supported phase widths including time-based 128-phase and 256-phase plus table offset; resource control provides load-table request, arbitration selector, channel identifier and enable; resource status provides table-loaded and negotiation-pending flags.

Power-budgeting select, data and capability registers live at offsets 0x04, 0x08 and 0x0c with total size 0x10. The data word packs base power in the low byte, scale, power-management substate and state, usage type and rail selectors in successive bit groups; the capability word carries an in-system-budget flag.

Root-complex event-collector association bitmap lives at offset 4 and associated bus numbers at offset 8, where the bus word carries a minimum version of 2 plus next and last bus-number bytes. The vendor-specific extended header at offset 4 packs a 16-bit vendor identifier, 4-bit revision and 12-bit length in ascending bit order.

HyperTransport capabilities use 3-bit and wider masks to classify type codes: slave/primary and host/secondary link codes under the narrow mask, and interrupt, 40- and 64-bit remapping, unit-ID clumping, extended-config, message-signaled-interrupt mapping, direct route, channel set, error retry, generation-3 and power-management codes under the wider mask. Message mapping provides a flags offset with mapping-enable and fixed-only bits, a fixed APIC-style base address, low and high address offsets, and a low-address mask. Capability structure sizes are 28 bytes for long slave/primary form and 24 bytes for short host/secondary form.
